speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to determine the cause, have you experienced any fever, chills, or nausea alongside these symptoms? Also, how would you describe the nature of the pain—is it constant or does it come in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). Your history of recurrent UTIs and the sudden onset of visible hematuria with flank pain is highly suggestive of a stone, though a renal ultrasound or non-contrast CT would be needed to confirm the size and location of any obstruction.
